cards.q: What is a safe following distance?
cards.a: At least three seconds in good weather. Increase the gap in rain, darkness and icy conditions.

cards.q: What does a triangular sign mean?
cards.a: Warning: there is a hazard or a change in conditions ahead.

cards.q: What does a round sign mean?
cards.a: Prohibition, obligation or restriction, such as a speed limit.

cards.q: What should you do at a stop sign?
cards.a: Stop completely, check both directions and only then move off when it is safe.

cards.q: What is the blind spot?
cards.a: The area the mirrors do not cover. That is why you must glance over your shoulder before changing lane.

cards.q: In what order do you check before changing lane?
cards.a: Mirror, then over your shoulder, then indicate in good time – and then change lane.

cards.q: What should you do when entering a roundabout?
cards.a: Slow down, give way to those already inside it and choose your lane early.

cards.q: When do you signal when leaving a roundabout?
cards.a: In good time, before you leave the roundabout.

cards.q: How do you best join a motorway?
cards.a: Use the slip road to build speed and match the traffic, then check your mirror and look over your shoulder.

cards.q: Which lane should you be in on a motorway?
cards.a: The right-hand lane when you are not overtaking.

cards.q: What should you check before setting off?
cards.a: Seat, mirrors, seat belts, lights, wipers and that the windows are clean.

cards.q: May you use your phone while driving?
cards.a: Not unless it is hands-free – even a short message takes your attention off the road.

cards.q: What should you do in the dark?
cards.a: Use your lights, keep the windows clean, drive more slowly and look further ahead.

cards.q: What should you do on a wet or icy road?
cards.a: Increase the distance, reduce speed and brake gently and earlier than usual.

cards.q: What is defensive driving?
cards.a: Seeing hazards in advance, looking far ahead, allowing for other people's mistakes and always having an escape route.

cards.q: How far ahead should you look?
What is a common mistake in a roundabout?
cards.a: Entering too fast and deciding too late which exit to take.

cards.q: What is assessed in the driving test?
cards.a: Safe and steady driving, observation, roundabouts, speed control, understanding of signs and communication in traffic.

cards.q: What should you do before the driving test?
cards.a: Go over the material and the checklist, check the car, arrive on time with your documents and rest well.

cards.q: May you drive faster than the speed limit?
cards.a: No. The speed limit is a ceiling, not a target – your speed must always suit the conditions.

cards.q: What should you do if something unexpected happens in the car?
cards.a: Stop in a safe place before making a decision.

cards.q: What should you do when a car is pulling out of a side road?
cards.a: Give yourself room and keep an escape route in case it does not give way.

cards.q: What is good to do after every lesson?
cards.a: Go over what went well, what needs more practice and book the next lesson.

cards.q: What matters in communication with other road users?
cards.a: Clear signals in good time, consideration and allowing for other people's mistakes.

cards.q: True or false? A police officer can take over control of traffic from the traffic lights.
True or false? The right-hand rule applies when there are no signs.
True or false? A driver always has priority if they are on the bigger road.
True or false? A stop sign works exactly like a give-way sign.
True or false? Parking on a pedestrian crossing is not permitted.
True or false? It is permitted to stop a vehicle in the middle of the road if there is no traffic.
True or false? Pedestrians always have priority on a pedestrian crossing.
True or false? A valid driving licence is needed to drive.
True or false? You can lose your driving licence because of traffic offences.
True or false? Worn tyres have no effect on how the car handles.
True or false? Once you have passed the driving test you do not need to renew your licence.
True or false? The car lights only need to be used in the dark.
True or false? It is always safe to drive at the speed limit.
True or false? Stopping distance increases with speed.
True or false? A car takes longer to stop on a wet road.
True or false? Emotional factors such as anger have no effect on driving.
True or false? Overtaking is always allowed, but you must always take care.
True or false? If you take the driving test in an automatic car you may drive any car.
True or false? You may begin your driving lessons at any time after your sixteenth birthday.
True or false? A give-way sign can be marked on the road surface.
True or false? ABS brakes work so that the car can still be steered even when braking hard.
True or false? If a car is towing a trailer it does not matter whether the trailer has lights at the rear.
True or false? An airbag warning light comes on in the dashboard if the airbags are not working.
True or false? You may use the horn to tell other road users off.
True or false? A driver should look in the rear-view mirror when stopping or slowing down suddenly.
True or false? You must not stop a vehicle in a roundabout.
True or false? If speed is doubled, braking distance is also doubled.
True or false? Hazard lights should be used to warn other drivers about police traffic.
True or false? Road users have no obligation to help if they come to an accident.
True or false? A driver may drive if their blood alcohol level measures under 0.8%.
True or false? A full driving licence is valid for 15 years.
True or false? A driver approaching a roundabout must give way to those already in it.
True or false? A vehicle may never be moved at the scene of an accident.
True or false? The driver must make sure that a passenger under 15 uses safety and protection equipment.
True or false? You must not use a phone while driving without hands-free equipment.
True or false? It is important to take conditions into account, but the driver's field of vision does not shrink as speed increases.
True or false? Whoever arrives first at a junction has priority.
True or false? Motor traffic on footpaths is strictly forbidden.
True or false? Direction signs are always yellow.
True or false? The Icelandic Transport Authority issues driving licences for category B.
True or false? Car accidents can be prevented by pulling hard on the brake pads.
True or false? A seat belt does not have to be worn when reversing.
True or false? The law says that eating while driving is not permitted.
True or false? Penalty points expire after 3 years.
True or false? By law a learner driver must attend at least one 4-hour first aid course.
True or false? If an accident happens on a main road, a warning triangle must be put out.
True or false? If a car is damaged in a collision but the airbags have not gone off, you can assume they cannot go off.
True or false? With a category B licence you may carry 8 passengers.
True or false? The outer lane in a roundabout always has the right of way.
True or false? The cogwheel method is a rule everyone must follow in roundabouts.
Which class of traffic signs is round with a white border, a white symbol and a blue background? · A) Mandatory signs · B) Information signs · C) Priority signs
What is the first thing to do when arriving at a car accident?
When overtaking a cyclist, the gap must not be less than? · A) 1 metre · B) 1.5 metres · C) 2 metres
The first driving licence is a provisional licence. How long is it valid and when can it be renewed?
cards.a: It is valid for three years and can be renewed after 1 year.

cards.q: When may you begin driving lessons in Iceland?
cards.a: At the earliest on your sixteenth birthday.

cards.q: When may fog lights be used? · A) Only when it is foggy or snowing · B) Only outside built-up areas in fog, rain or drifting snow · C) When the driver considers them necessary
cards.a: B) Only outside built-up areas in fog, rain or drifting snow.

cards.q: What is the blind spot? · A) The area the driver cannot see without moving their head · B) The area directly in front of the car that the lights do not reach · C) The area directly behind the car
cards.a: A) The area the driver cannot see without moving their head.

cards.q: When is a car considered parked? · A) When it is in a parking space · B) When nobody is inside the car · C) When the car has been stationary for 3 minutes
cards.a: C) When the car has been stationary for 3 minutes.

cards.q: What is the speed limit on a gravel road outside built-up areas? · A) 70 km/h · B) 80 km/h · C) 90 km/h
What does a half-broken dividing line (short gaps between the lines) mean?
cards.a: That it is permitted to cross the dividing line with care.

cards.q: What is at the top of the hierarchy of control? · A) The police · B) The signs and the traffic law · C) The traffic lights
What is the speed limit in a home zone? · A) 15 km/h · B) 20 km/h · C) 30 km/h
When is it not permitted to change lane? · A) When there is a broken line on the road · B) When there is heavy traffic · C) In a roundabout
How many driving lessons must a learner take at a minimum before being allowed to practise driving?
Who has overall control of traffic matters in Iceland? · A) The police · B) Parliament · C) The Ministry of Infrastructure
How many classes of traffic signs are there? · A) 5 · B) 7 · C) 9
What is the driver's field of vision when stationary? · A) 180° · B) 120° · C) 150°
What is the driver's field of vision at 60 km/h? · A) about 104° · B) about 42° · C) about 70°

What are supplementary plates? · A) Signs below a main sign giving clearer instructions · B) Signs under a car with information about it · C) Signs that let you know when you are entering an underpass
cards.a: A) Signs below a main sign giving clearer instructions.

cards.q: How fast may you drive in the Hvalfjörður tunnel? · A) 70 km/h · B) 80 km/h · C) 90 km/h
When must the car lights be on? · A) When it is dark · B) Always · C) When it is foggy
What are speed bumps for? · A) To annoy people · B) To make drivers slow down · C) To treat the vehicle well
cards.a: B) To make drivers slow down.

cards.q: Which route around Iceland is shorter? · A) The northern route · B) The southern route · C) They are equally long
What are the colours of the no parking sign? · A) Blue and red · B) Red and yellow · C) Red and white
How does the give-way sign point? · A) A triangle pointing up · B) A triangle pointing down · C) The sign is round
How long is the Hvalfjörður tunnel? · A) 4520 metres · B) 5770 metres · C) 6570 metres
How old must you be to ride a light moped?
What is the fine if you drive at 105 km/h where the limit is 90 km/h? · A) 50,000 ISK · B) 70,000 ISK · C) 100,000 ISK
What is the fine if you drive at 170 km/h where the limit is 90 km/h? · A) 200,000 ISK · B) 250,000 ISK · C) 300,000 ISK
What is the fine for driving through a red light? · A) 40,000 ISK · B) 50,000 ISK · C) 60,000 ISK
Which insurance is compulsory for a car?
cards.a: Personal accident insurance for the driver and third-party liability insurance for the vehicle.

cards.q: What is stopping distance?
cards.a: Reaction distance and braking distance combined.

cards.q: During which period may you drive on studded tyres?
During which period is it not permitted to drive on studded tyres?
If you drive a car weighing 2.5 tonnes, what load may you tow on a trailer with a category B licence only? · A) 750 kg · B) 1000 kg · C) 1250 kg
What is the minimum tread depth for winter tyres? · A) 1.6 mm · B) 2.5 mm · C) 3 mm
What is the minimum tread depth for summer tyres? · A) 1.2 mm · B) 1.6 mm · C) 2.5 mm
Can you take a driving assessment in your own car?
cards.a: Yes, you may take a driving assessment in your own car.

cards.q: When do cars with personalised plates have to be inspected?
How fast may you drive when towing a car with a tow rope? · A) At the speed limit of the road · B) 50 km/h · C) 30 km/h
What are the car mirrors for? · A) To keep an eye on nearby traffic · B) To watch a child in the back seat · C) To look at yourself
cards.a: A) To keep an eye on nearby traffic.

cards.q: Which traffic sign is usually used up at car height? · A) The warning sign for other danger · B) A mandatory direction sign · C) A warning sign with a blind summit plate
May you drive a tractor with a category B licence?
What should you do if the oil light comes on while driving? · A) Drive to the nearest garage · B) Stop the car and switch off the engine · C) Have the car serviced at the next opportunity
cards.a: B) Stop the car and switch off the engine.

cards.q: What should you do if the temperature light comes on? · A) Throw cold water over the engine · B) Stop the car and switch off the engine · C) Turn on the heater
cards.a: B) Stop the car and switch off the engine.

cards.q: What is the most dangerous gas in car exhaust? · A) Carbon monoxide · B) Water vapour · C) Methane
What is the purpose of airbags?
cards.a: To reduce the chance of people being injured in a traffic accident.

cards.q: What blood alcohol level is permitted if you intend to drive? · A) 0.0% · B) 0.2% · C) 0.8%
Can a doctor affect the renewal of a driving licence?
cards.a: Yes, because a medical certificate is needed to renew a driving licence.

cards.q: How tall must a person be to sit in the front seat?
How do new drivers generally assess their own ability?
cards.a: Most new drivers overestimate their ability and underestimate the danger that lurks in traffic.

cards.q: What does a warning sign look like and what is its purpose?
cards.a: A warning sign is an equilateral triangle with a red border and a yellow centre. Warning signs are intended to draw attention to a hazard.

cards.q: What are road marker posts for and how do their reflectors work?
cards.a: Marker posts mark the edge of the road. The post on the left has two reflector lines pointing towards the road, while on the right there is one reflector line pointing towards the road.

cards.q: Since which year has wearing a seat belt been required by law in Iceland?
cards.a: Seat belt use has been required by law in Iceland since 1981.

cards.q: What difference could a seat belt have made in many car accidents?
cards.a: In many car accidents a seat belt would have saved a life if it had been used.

cards.q: When did the first car arrive in Iceland and what kind of car was it?
cards.a: The first car was imported to Iceland in 1904. It was a French-German Cudell, model year 1900.

cards.q: How long does it take to become a relatively safe driver?
cards.a: It takes about 5 to 7 years to become a relatively safe driver.

cards.q: What effect does overpowering music in the car have on driving?
cards.a: Drivers who play overpowering music in the car make 25% more driving errors than those with no extra distraction.

cards.q: How dangerous is fatigue and drowsiness in a driver?
cards.a: Fatigue and drowsiness in a driver can be very dangerous and even fatal. Tired drivers who get behind the wheel create a dangerous situation in traffic.

cards.q: How should an automatic car be towed?
cards.a: If an automatic car has to be towed it should only be towed a short distance at low speed in a safe area away from traffic.

cards.q: Who is responsible for the passengers in a car?
cards.a: Everyone travelling as a passenger is in the care of the driver, who is responsible for them.

cards.q: What is a good thing to do if you notice a car driving without lights?
cards.a: If you notice that a car has no lights on, it is good to flash your own lights to let the other driver know they have forgotten to switch them on.

cards.q: What should you do if the light turns amber when you are close to the stop line?
cards.a: If you are so close to the stop line when the amber light comes on that you cannot stop the car without creating danger, you should drive across the junction.

cards.q: What responsibility does the driver have for the car's safety equipment?
cards.a: As the driver you are responsible for making sure the car's safety equipment is in order and that passengers use it.

cards.q: May children under 150 cm sit in a front seat with an active airbag?
cards.a: Children shorter than 150 cm must not be passengers in a front seat with an active inflatable airbag.

cards.q: What does a red triangle on medicine boxes mean?
cards.a: A red triangle on medicine boxes means that you should avoid driving while taking that medicine.

cards.q: What happens if an Icelander commits a serious traffic offence abroad?
cards.a: Icelandic police cooperate with police in other countries. If a person commits a serious traffic offence abroad they also lose their driving rights here in Iceland.

cards.q: How large a share of the information in traffic comes through sight?
cards.a: Good eyesight is very important for a driver, as about 90% of the information from traffic is received through sight.

cards.q: What effect does off-road driving have on Icelandic nature?
cards.a: Iceland is a fragile country and off-road driving can leave wheel ruts that heal slowly or never.

cards.q: Why must a car engine never be left running in a closed space?
cards.a: A car engine must never be left running in a closed space, because the carbon monoxide in the exhaust causes death within a short time.

cards.q: What effect does unnecessary idling have on the environment?
cards.a: Do not keep the car running unnecessarily. It pollutes the air.

cards.q: When can the sun blind drivers?
cards.a: When the sun is low in spring and autumn it can blind drivers.

cards.q: When should a driver avoid overtaking?
cards.a: In fog, heavy rain or drifting snow a driver should preferably not attempt to overtake.

cards.q: Must motor vehicles in traffic be insured in Iceland?
cards.a: In Iceland it is compulsory to insure all motor vehicles that are in traffic.

cards.q: What do studies show about using a mobile phone while driving?
cards.a: Studies show that using a mobile phone while driving increases the risk of incidents and accidents, even when hands-free equipment is used.

cards.q: What is important in dense, heavy traffic?
cards.a: In dense and heavy traffic it is important to stay calm and not let other drivers distract you, which can create danger.

cards.q: Why is it important to use the indicators a lot?
cards.a: It is important to use the indicators a lot to let other drivers know what you intend to do.

cards.q: What should be kept in mind when driving across a junction?
cards.a: Do not blindly trust other drivers when driving across a junction. Always be careful and keep an eye on the traffic.

cards.q: Why is it not good to drive much slower than the speed limit in the left lane?
cards.a: It is not good to drive much slower than the speed limit in the left lane of a road with two lanes in the same direction.

cards.q: What is one of the most dangerous breaches of the traffic rules?
cards.a: One of the most dangerous breaches of the traffic rules is overtaking just before reaching a pedestrian crossing or at one.
